occlusion_reveal_distance — DRIVE traffic op

• Data kinds: any → scalar

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.occlusion_reveal_distance(ego_xy, ego_heading: 'float', parked_box, emerge_xy) -> 'float' (to call the implementation directly, import drivetraffic; drivetraffic.occlusion_reveal_distance(ego_xy, ego_heading: 'float', parked_box, emerge_xy) -> 'float'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("occlusion_reveal_distance"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Longitudinal distance at which a point emerge_xy hidden behind a car parked at the roadside (an oriented box) becomes visible for the first time from the ego vehicle's eye.

The ego vehicle's eye moves along p(s) = ego_xy + s h (h = (cos ψ, sin ψ), s ≥ 0 = forward travel). It sees e if the line of sight = the segment p(s) → e does not pass through the interior of the box. Since the box is convex, the "not visible s" form an interval, whose ends are where the line of sight grazes a corner of the box or where the path crosses an edge of the box. For each corner c, the intersection s_c of the line e + λ(c − e) with the path is solved as a 2×2 system (closed form); the candidates {0, s_c, intersections of the path with the edges} are checked for visibility in increasing order, and at the first visible s*, d = h · (e − p(s*)) is returned.

Axis-parallel example (path y = 0, heading +x, shadowing corner c, e beyond the box): d = (e_x − c_x) · e_y / (e_y − c_y).

parked_box = (cx, cy, length, width, yaw) (centre, overall length, overall width, heading). If visible from the start, the longitudinal distance at s* = 0; if never visible however far one travels (e inside the box), inf. A negative d (e already passed by the time it becomes visible) is returned as is. A line of sight grazing a corner counts as "visible" (the box is shrunk by just 1e-9 relative before testing so that floating-point jitter does not split the decision).

Raises ValueError: shape, non-finite, dimension ≤ 0.
